extracted.intended_audience: writers and literary agents/editors using the Manuscript Wish List (MSWL) platform
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for writers, agents, and editors on using ManuscriptWishList.com and the #MSWL hashtag—including who may post, how to submit work, account/password policies, content standards, and the website's legal Terms of Use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may post on #MSWL and ManuscriptWishList.com
rubrics_metrics.description: Only agents and editors post on #MSWL and ManuscriptWishList.com; it exists for agents/editors to post what they wish they had in their inbox so writers can search for compatible people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should NOT post on the hashtag — doing so is unlikely to help and may annoy agents. Asking an agent a question (e.g., clarifying a genre preference) is acceptable; do not use the hashtag for pitches. If you must reference the tag, say “I saw that you posted on MSWL.”

rubrics_metrics.name: How to reference MSWL in social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use the #MSWL hashtag in tweets as a writer; instead reference that you 'saw that you posted on MSWL' if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cluttering the feed; agents mostly read the tag and will be annoyed if rules are broken, which may reflect poorly on you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting to agents/editors who accept direct submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agent/editor includes their submissions email or accepts direct submissions, you should go to their agency/publisher site, look up their submission guidelines, and follow those guidelines—usually an emailed query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not leave your pitch in the ManuscriptWishList comments; the site will not post pitches and the agent/editor will not see them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting to editors who only take agented submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an editor only accepts agented submissions, you must first find an agent to submit to that editor; do not submit directly to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting directly when an editor requires agented submissions could result in that editor being removed from the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence on agents/editors' legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: You should research any agent/editor: Google them, check Preditors & Editors, Absolute Write, and Publishers Marketplace, and ask if the agent adheres to the AAR Cannon of Ethics. Speak with a current client or ask for a referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site cannot guarantee every profile is reputable; these steps improve your odds and protect you. The site tries to ensure profiles are professional but is not responsible for users' actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No forwarding/introductions by site staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The site will not forward a note to an editor or act as a direct agent/introducer on behalf of writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should not ask the site to forward notes; the site is not comfortable doing that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after prior rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, if an agent already rejected your work, you should not resubmit even if you see the agent requesting similar work—an agent’s answer usually stands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only resubmit if the agent explicitly says they are open to seeing works a second time via #MSWL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password access for certain posts is agent/editor-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Password-protected posts are available and the password is only for agents and editors; the site verifies identity before sending the password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Password protection exists because some editors who do not accept unagented submissions prefer their information restricted. To get the password you must join and be verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent/editor control over contact information visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Including contact information on a profile is up to the agent or editor; if they opt out, the site will respect that choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contact info isn't listed, Google '[Name] submission guidelines' or consult the agency/publisher site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents/editors eligibility to join the site
rubrics_metrics.description: All agents and editors with an @YourCompanyName.com email address can apply to be listed; use the form on the Join page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ongoing project—it's not too late to submit a listing. Registration packet includes instructions for creating/updating profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents/editors should update listings as needs change
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents and editors can and should update their listing when their needs change; version 3.0/4.0 enables each agent/editor to have login credentials for easy updating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you receive your registration packet, it will include instructions to create and update your profile. Updating is easy and encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password-protected posts recommended for editors who take agented submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors who do not accept unagented submissions are recommended to password-protect their posts so only agents and editors see their contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Password protection prevents unwanted direct contacts from writers who should go through agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and update turnaround expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Though much of version 4.0 is automated, humans still approve new accounts and profile updates, so posting/updating may take time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please have patience; if something is urgent, email the provided contact address for assistance.
